paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is shouting at us: God's plan does not break when evil shows up. Herod is filled with rage and sends orders to put to death all the boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity who were two years old and under (Matthew 2:16). I think that is the heaviest part of this whole passage, and I won't dress it up. But the angel had already warned Joseph, and the Child was already on the road to Egypt (Matthew 2:13-14).

Now look at how Matthew keeps pointing back. "Out of Egypt I called My Son" (Matthew 2:15). Rachel weeping in Ramah, long before any of this (Matthew 2:17-18). "He will be called a Nazarene" (Matthew 2:23). Matthew is telling us that none of this caught God off guard, and that what He spoke through the prophets was being carried out right here. Even the weeping in Ramah, which Matthew says was spoken through the prophet Jeremiah, was not a surprise to Him.

So what do you do with that, baker? You do what Joseph did. Twice the angel says "Get up!" and twice Joseph gets up (Matthew 2:14, 21). I need a sticky note and a prayer just to take out the trash, but Joseph listens and moves. When the road gets strange, and it will, trust the One who is leading and take the next step He gives you. The story isn't over, either, because there is more of Jesus still to come.
